# truefoundry_gateway_rate_limiting_config (Resource)

Manages the AI gateway rate limiting configuration: how many requests or tokens matching requests may spend per period. Applied as a `gateway-rate-limiting-config` manifest via `PUT /api/svc/v1/apply`. **The rate limiting config is a tenant-wide singleton** — define at most one of this resource per control plane; an apply replaces all rules. Import the existing config with `terraform import truefoundry_gateway_rate_limiting_config.example gateway-rate-limiting-config`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The tenant-wide AI gateway rate limiting config (singleton — define at most
# one): how many requests or tokens matching requests may spend per period.
resource "truefoundry_gateway_rate_limiting_config" "limits" {
  name = "rate-limiting-config"

  rules = [
    # 60 requests per minute per user, on the models of one region.
    {
      id = "region-per-user"

      when = {
        models = ["my-azure-openai/gpt-4o", "my-azure-openai/gpt-4.1"]
      }

      limit_to = 60
      unit     = "requests_per_minute"

      # Buckets the counter per entity. Note these values differ from the
      # per-user/per-model spelling used by the budget resources.
      rate_limit_applies_per = ["user"]
    },

    # One shared daily token budget for everything a team sends.
    {
      id = "team-token-cap"

      when = {
        subjects = ["team:everyone"]
      }

      limit_to = 1000000
      unit     = "tokens_per_day"
    },

    # A separate hourly cap per app, keyed by a metadata value from the
    # X-TFY-METADATA header. At most two partitionings per rule.
    {
      id = "per-app-hourly"

      when = {
        metadata = { environment = "production" }
      }

      limit_to               = 5000
      unit                   = "requests_per_hour"
      rate_limit_applies_per = ["model", "metadata.appId"]
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the rate limiting config.
- `rules` (Attributes Set) Rate limiting rules. Every matching rule is enforced and a request is rejected if any of them is over its limit; order is not significant. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Control plane ID of the gateway rate limiting config.

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `id` (String) Identifier of this rule, unique within the config. 2-62 characters of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, and `{}`; must not start with a digit or end with a hyphen.
- `limit_to` (Number) Maximum number of requests or tokens per period, depending on `unit`.
- `unit` (String) What is counted, and over which period. One of: `requests_per_minute`, `requests_per_hour`, `requests_per_day`, `tokens_per_minute`, `tokens_per_hour`, `tokens_per_day`.
- `when` (Attributes) Requests this rule applies to; all given parts must match. An empty block (`{}`) matches every request. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--when))

Optional:

- `rate_limit_applies_per` (Set of String) Buckets the counter per entity instead of sharing one counter across all matching requests. One of: `user`, `virtualaccount`, `model`, or `metadata.<key>` (e.g. `metadata.appId`). At most 2 values. Note these differ from the `per-user`-style values of budget limiting v2.

<a id="nestedatt--rules--when"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.when`

Optional:

- `metadata` (Map of String) Request metadata key-value pairs to match, from the `X-TFY-METADATA` header.
- `models` (Set of String) Models to match, as `<provider-account>/<model>` names.
- `subjects` (Set of String) Subject FQNs to match, e.g. `user:someone@example.com` or `team:everyone`. The control plane rejects subjects that do not exist.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The rate limiting config is a tenant-wide singleton; its import ID is the
# fixed string "gateway-rate-limiting-config".
terraform import truefoundry_gateway_rate_limiting_config.limits gateway-rate-limiting-config
```
